q: Biology， as most people understand it， is the Science of ____.
e: Biology, as most people understand it, is the Science of Life. Biology is the science of life: plants, animals, and microorganisms. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: They regard it as the study of living things， such as plants， animals and ____.
e: They regard it as the study of living things, such as plants, animals and microorganisms. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi.

q: The whole world is now suffering under the impact of infectious disease outbreak and weather changes cause by the effect of ____.
e: The whole world is now suffering under the impact of infectious disease outbreak and weather changes cause by the effect of global warming. Global warming is the rise in earth's temperature from extra greenhouse gases.

q: Over fishing， over hunting and deforestation may lead to problems in feeding the world ____ population.
e: Over fishing, over hunting and deforestation may lead to problems in feeding the world exploding population. Overfishing, overhunting, and deforestation make it harder to feed an exploding human population. Deforestation removes forest and can wreck habitat and climate regulation.

q: Many species of plants and animals have disappeared ____.
e: Many species of plants and animals have disappeared forever. When a species is extinct it has disappeared forever. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Biology is concerned with animal breeding， agriculture and also in the field of ____ just to mention a few.
e: Biology is concerned with animal breeding, agriculture and also in the field of medicine just to mention a few. Applied biology includes medicine, which restores and maintains human health. Agriculture is crop farming; it is not the same as animal husbandry.

q: Examples include morphology， the study of structure and form of organisms and ____， the study of cell structure and function.
e: Examples include morphology, the study of structure and form of organisms and cytology, the study of cell structure and function. Cytology is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The applied biology includes ____ which is application of biology in productive industry， the medicine and veterinary science.
e: The applied biology includes biotechnology which is application of biology in productive industry, the medicine and veterinary science. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. Veterinary science restores and maintains animal health.

q: Biology has strong links with physics， chemistry， geology， geography， mathematics and ____， etc.
e: Biology has strong links with physics, chemistry, geology, geography, mathematics and computer science, etc. Biology also links to computer science, as well as physics and chemistry. Biology is the science of life, not art or history.

q: ____， for example， applies the laws of physics to study the biological processes， like flight of the bird or echolocation in bats.
e: Biophysics, for example, applies the laws of physics to study the biological processes, like flight of the bird or echolocation in bats. Biophysics applies physics to living processes, such as bird flight or bat echolocation. Bats use echolocation; biophysics studies that with the laws of physics.

q: ____ is the study of chemical substances and the chemical processes which occur in the cells and organisms.
e: Biochemistry is the study of chemical substances and the chemical processes which occur in the cells and organisms. Biochemistry studies chemical substances and reactions inside cells.

q: ____ explains how plants and animals are distributed on earth through space and time.
e: Biogeography explains how plants and animals are distributed on earth through space and time. Biogeography tracks distribution of species through space and time.

q: Dichotomous keys provide a simple way to put unknown organisms in their proper ____.
e: Dichotomous keys provide a simple way to put unknown organisms in their proper taxa. Taxa are the ranked groups used in hierarchical classification. A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific.

q: The word dichotomous is derived from Greek words meaning "divided into two ____".
e: The word dichotomous is derived from Greek words meaning "divided into two parts ". A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: The method of dichotomous keys is to divide the groups of organisms into two ____ repeatedly.
e: The method of dichotomous keys is to divide the groups of organisms into two categories repeatedly. A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: They often begin with general characteristics and then progress to more ____ ones step by step.
e: They often begin with general characteristics and then progress to more specific ones step by step. Enzymes are specific: each active site fits a limited set of substrates.

q: By following the sequence of the given dichotomous keys and making the correct choices the unknown organisms can be identified and placed in their proper ____ level.
e: By following the sequence of the given dichotomous keys and making the correct choices the unknown organisms can be identified and placed in their proper taxonomic level. A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific.

q: Vascular system absent ____
e: Vascular system absent 2. A vascular system of xylem and phloem is missing in bryophytes.

q: Vascular system present ____
e: Vascular system present 3. A vascular system of xylem and phloem is missing in bryophytes.

q: No embryo formation ..... ____
e: No embryo formation Thallophyta. Thallophytes have a simple body with no true embryo in the classical scheme. A true embryo is part of the higher-plant life cycle; thallophytes were defined without that.

q: Has spores and gametes formation ____
e: Has spores and gametes formation Bryophyta. Bryophytes are non-vascular plants such as mosses. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis.

q: Spore-bearing... ____
e: Spore-bearing Pteridophyta. Pteridophytes are vascular, seedless plants such as ferns. Ferns and mosses spread by spores, not by flowers.

q: Seed-bearing........ ____
e: Seed-bearing 4. Seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms.

q: Non-flowering plants........ ____
e: Non-flowering plants Gymnospermae. Gymnosperms have vascular tissue and seeds but do not make flowers. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms.

q: Flowering plants .. ____
e: Flowering plants. Angiospermae. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms.

q: Cold-blooded animals Warm-blooded animals ____
e: Cold-blooded animals Warm-blooded animals 2. 2 is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Body covered with scales. ____
e: Body covered with scales. 4. Scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys.

q: Body not covered with scales. ____
e: Body not covered with scales. Amphibian. Amphibians can use skin, mouth lining, and lungs for gas exchange. Scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys.

q: Feathers present on body ..............____
e: Feathers present on body Bird. Birds are warm-blooded vertebrates with feathers, not fur. Feathers mark birds in a vertebrate key, not mammals.

q: Hair present on body ____
e: Hair present on body Mammal. Mammals are warm-blooded vertebrates with hair and milk. Hair or fur is a mammal feature in simple vertebrate keys.

q: Has fins ____
e: Has fins Fish. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces.

q: Has four limbs or without limbs.. ____
e: Has four limbs or without limbs. Reptile. Reptiles are scaly, air-breathing vertebrates that usually use lungs. Four major environment components together are called the ecosphere.

q: Identification in biology is the process in which an organism or specimen is classified and assigned a scientific ____.
e: Identification in biology is the process in which an organism or specimen is classified and assigned a scientific name. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: The study and process of classification is known as ____.
e: The study and process of classification is known as Taxonomy. Taxonomy is the science of naming and classifying organisms. Classification groups organisms so we can name them and see relatedness.

q: The classification or grouping of living things is arranged in a hierarchical order and is known as ____ classification.
e: The classification or grouping of living things is arranged in a hierarchical order and is known as hierarchical classification. Living things are placed in a nested hierarchy of taxa. Classification groups organisms so we can name them and see relatedness.

q: At the top of the hierarchical are three domains， Archaea，Bacteria and ____.
e: At the top of the hierarchical are three domains, Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya. Eukarya are organisms whose cells have a true nucleus. Living things are placed in a nested hierarchy of taxa.

q: Each of the three domains is subdivided into seven different levels or taxa - they are Kingdom， Phylum/Division，Class， Order， Family， Genus and ____.
e: Each of the three domains is subdivided into seven different levels or taxa - they are Kingdom, Phylum/Division, Class, Order, Family, Genus and Species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring. Older schemes listed seven ranks; adding domain makes eight.

q: Another method of classification known as ____ is also used by modern taxonomists.
e: Another method of classification known as cladistics is also used by modern taxonomists. Cladistics groups organisms by shared derived characters and common ancestry. Classification groups organisms so we can name them and see relatedness.

q: In this method of classification many techniques are used including comparing of ____ from different species to find out how closely they are related.
e: In this method of classification many techniques are used including comparing of DNA from different species to find out how closely they are related. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. Classification groups organisms so we can name them and see relatedness.

q: To carry out the identification of organism， biologists usually use easily identifiable features like morphology and ____ as keys.
e: To carry out the identification of organism, biologists usually use easily identifiable features like morphology and anatomy as keys. Anatomy studies internal structure of organisms. Morphology is the study of structure and form of organisms.

q: Keys provide a simple way to ____ organisms.
e: Keys provide a simple way to classify organisms. Classify is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Among the most widely used tools in biology are ____.
e: Among the most widely used tools in biology are microscopes. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: Biologists use these to study cells， cell parts and also organisms that are too small to be seen with naked ____.
e: Biologists use these to study cells, cell parts and also organisms that are too small to be seen with naked eyes. Eyes is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Basically there are two main types of microscope， the light microscope and the ____ microscope.
e: Basically there are two main types of microscope, the light microscope and the electron microscope. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam. A light microscope uses light as the radiation that forms the image.

q: The light microscope uses light as a source of radiation to form the image of the specimen being studied while the electron microscope uses ____.
e: The light microscope uses light as a source of radiation to form the image of the specimen being studied while the electron microscope uses electron. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam. A light microscope uses light as the radiation that forms the image.

q: Two different types of electron microscopes are commonly used - the transmission electron microscope or TEM and the scanning electron microscope or ____.
e: Two different types of electron microscopes are commonly used - the transmission electron microscope or TEM and the scanning electron microscope or SEM. SEM scans the surface with electrons to give a three-dimensional view. Electron microscopes use electrons as the radiation source.

q: In the TEM， electron is passed through the specimen and allow us to see thin sections of the specimen， and thus the inside ____.
e: In the TEM, electron is passed through the specimen and allow us to see thin sections of the specimen, and thus the inside cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: In SEM the electron beam is passed back and forth over the surface of the specimen. Only the reflected beam is observed and ____ appearance is obtained.
e: In SEM the electron beam is passed back and forth over the surface of the specimen. Only the reflected beam is observed and three dimensional appearance is obtained. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts. Observed size over actual size gives magnification.

q: Usually substage illumination is the light ____.
e: Usually substage illumination is the light source. Source is the biological term this statement needs.

q: By adjusting the iris diaphragm， the amount of light reaching the specimen is ____.
e: By adjusting the iris diaphragm, the amount of light reaching the specimen is controlled. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. The iris diaphragm controls the amount of light reaching the specimen.

q: Condenser focuses the light onto the specimen on the ____.
e: Condenser focuses the light onto the specimen on the slide. The condenser focuses light onto the specimen; an iris diaphragm controls how much light.

q: Light passing through the specimen is collected by the objective lens and a magnified image is ____.
e: Light passing through the specimen is collected by the objective lens and a magnified image is produced. The objective lens both magnifies and provides resolving power.

q: This lens is responsible for both the magnification and ____.
e: This lens is responsible for both the magnification and resolution. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object.

q: Eyepiece lens magnifies but does not resolve the image formed by the objective ____.
e: Eyepiece lens magnifies but does not resolve the image formed by the objective lens. The objective lens both magnifies and provides resolving power. The eyepiece magnifies the image the objective has already formed; it does not set resolution.

q: Eyepiece lens focuses the image onto the ____.
e: Eyepiece lens focuses the image onto the eye. The eyepiece magnifies the image the objective has already formed; it does not set resolution.

q: The electron beam， the specimen and the fluorescent screen must be in the ____.
e: The electron beam, the specimen and the fluorescent screen must be in the vacuum. Electron beams travel in a vacuum, so EM specimens must be specially prepared. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: Electron gun and anode emit high velocity electron ____.
e: Electron gun and anode emit high velocity electron beam. SEM scans a beam back and forth over the surface; TEM sends the beam through the specimen. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses the electron beam onto the ____.
e: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses the electron beam onto the specimen. The condenser focuses light onto the specimen; an iris diaphragm controls how much light. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: Objective electromagnetic lens focuses and magnified the first ____.
e: Objective electromagnetic lens focuses and magnified the first image. The image is the observed size in the microscope. The objective lens both magnifies and provides resolving power.

q: Projector electromagnetic lenses focus the magnified image onto the ____.
e: Projector electromagnetic lenses focus the magnified image onto the screen. In TEM, projector lenses throw the final image onto a screen.

q: The image of the specimen in black and white is recorded on the screen or photographic ____.
e: The image of the specimen in black and white is recorded on the screen or photographic plate. Plate is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Uses light as a source of radiation. Uses ____ as a source of radiation.
e: Uses light as a source of radiation. Uses electron as a source of radiation. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: The image is projected on the eye or on photographic film. The image is projected on a screen or on photographic ____.
e: The image is projected on the eye or on photographic film. Film is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Preparation of specimen simple， not complicated. Preparation of specimen lengthy and ____.
e: Preparation of specimen simple, not complicated. Preparation of specimen lengthy and complicated.

q: Magnifies up to 2000X Magnifies up to ____ X
e: Magnifies up to 2000X Magnifies up to 500,000 X. 500,000 is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Either dead or alive specimen can be examined. Only dehydrated and dead specimen can be ____.
e: Either dead or alive specimen can be examined. Only dehydrated and dead specimen can be examined.

q: Inexpensive to purchase and operate. Expensive to purchase and ____.
e: Inexpensive to purchase and operate. Expensive to purchase and operate.

q: Magnification is the ability to increase the size of the image of the object being studied so that microscopic organisms become ____.
e: Magnification is the ability to increase the size of the image of the object being studied so that microscopic organisms become visible. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object.

q: Magnification can also be defined as the number of times larger an image is， compared with the real size of the ____.
e: Magnification can also be defined as the number of times larger an image is, compared with the real size of the object. In magnification, the object is the actual specimen size. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object.

q: Resolution is the ability to distinguish between two objects that are close ____.
e: Resolution is the ability to distinguish between two objects that are close together. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: If the two objects cannot be resolved they will be seen as a single ____.
e: If the two objects cannot be resolved they will be seen as a single object. In magnification, the object is the actual specimen size. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Resolving power shows up the smallest detail that a microscope can resolve when imaging an ____.
e: Resolving power shows up the smallest detail that a microscope can resolve when imaging an object. In magnification, the object is the actual specimen size. A microscope magnifies a specimen so hidden cell detail can be seen.

q: An increase in magnification does not always produce a more detail image. It might increases in size but not in ____.
e: An increase in magnification does not always produce a more detail image. It might increases in size but not in detail. Extra magnification without resolution does not add true detail, only a bigger blur. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object.

q: But with resolution， the greater the resolution， the greater the ____.
e: But with resolution, the greater the resolution, the greater the detail. Extra magnification without resolution does not add true detail, only a bigger blur. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate.

q: Biotechnology is a branch of applied biology which combines biological sciences with engineering ____.
e: Biotechnology is a branch of applied biology which combines biological sciences with engineering technologies. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: Biotechnology is a technology which apply the use of living systems and organisms to produce useful chemicals and products or to carry out industrial work for ____.
e: Biotechnology is a technology which apply the use of living systems and organisms to produce useful chemicals and products or to carry out industrial work for mankind. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture.

q: Although this branch of biology is well-known technology of our modern world， our ancestors had been practicing it for hundreds of years making wine， bread， cheese and breeding livestock and crops without any scientific ____.
e: Although this branch of biology is well-known technology of our modern world, our ancestors had been practicing it for hundreds of years making wine, bread, cheese and breeding livestock and crops without any scientific knowledge. Animal husbandry raises livestock for food and other products. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: It can be said that traditional biotechnology came into use thousands of years ago when people unknowingly discovered the usefulness of' microorganisms like bacteria and ____.
e: It can be said that traditional biotechnology came into use thousands of years ago when people unknowingly discovered the usefulness of' microorganisms like bacteria and yeast. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi.

q: It was known that seven thousand years ago， people in Mesopotamia used bacteria to convert wine into ____.
e: It was known that seven thousand years ago, people in Mesopotamia used bacteria to convert wine into vinegar. Older schemes listed seven ranks; adding domain makes eight. Wine yeast uses oxygen first, then ferments anaerobically when oxygen is gone.

q: Examples of this traditional biotechnology includes making wine， cheese， yoghurt， bread and ____.
e: Examples of this traditional biotechnology includes making wine, cheese, yoghurt, bread and beer. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. In bread making, yeast produces carbon dioxide, which makes dough rise, plus ethanol.

q: The scientific study of the biochemical processes that has developed in the past few decades contributes much to the advancement of the ____.
e: The scientific study of the biochemical processes that has developed in the past few decades contributes much to the advancement of the biotechnology. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture.

q: Nowadays， with the development of gene technology scientists are able to modify or manipulate living organisms by transferring genes from one organism to another， usually an unrelated ____.
e: Nowadays, with the development of gene technology scientists are able to modify or manipulate living organisms by transferring genes from one organism to another, usually an unrelated species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock.

q: In this way genes for herbicides resistance are put into crop plants and human insulin producing genes are put into bacteria and cultured to produce ____.
e: In this way genes for herbicides resistance are put into crop plants and human insulin producing genes are put into bacteria and cultured to produce insulin. Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar.

q: Genetic engineering carried out on some plants and animals have enabled them to produce substances that are not part of their normal ____.
e: Genetic engineering carried out on some plants and animals have enabled them to produce substances that are not part of their normal metabolism. Metabolism is the biological term this statement needs.

q: They are known as transgenic plants and ____.
e: They are known as transgenic plants and animals. Animals is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Transgenic goats produce antibodies and blood clotting agent in their ____.
e: Transgenic goats produce antibodies and blood clotting agent in their milk. Blood clotting seals wounds and needs clotting proteins from the liver.

q: Transgenic plants are engineered to produce ____.
e: Transgenic plants are engineered to produce vaccine. Vaccines are an applied-biology tool for preventing infectious disease.

q: Microorganisms or microbes are small organisms that can only be seen with the ____.
e: Microorganisms or microbes are small organisms that can only be seen with the microscope. A microscope magnifies a specimen so hidden cell detail can be seen. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi.

q: The term microorganisms include protists， archea， fungi， bacteria and ____.
e: The term microorganisms include protists, archea, fungi, bacteria and viruses. Viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi.

q: Of these， archea and bacteria are prokaryotes whereas protists and fungi are ____.
e: Of these, archea and bacteria are prokaryotes whereas protists and fungi are eukaryotes. Eukaryotes have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Prokaryotes such as bacteria and archaea lack a true nucleus.

q: The viruses are not cellular and they do not have the characteristic of living things but they can reproduce inside the living cell of other organisms by using the genetic materials of the ____.
e: The viruses are not cellular and they do not have the characteristic of living things but they can reproduce inside the living cell of other organisms by using the genetic materials of the host. Viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell.

q: Protists are single-celled organisms usually found in the wet ____.
e: Protists are single-celled organisms usually found in the wet surrounding. Surrounding is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Fungi have hyphae or filamentous cells but yeasts， an unusual family of fungi， have single spherical ____.
e: Fungi have hyphae or filamentous cells but yeasts, an unusual family of fungi, have single spherical cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells.

q: These microbes are harness by biotechnologists to run their biotechnological processes in manufacturing useful products for ____.
e: These microbes are harness by biotechnologists to run their biotechnological processes in manufacturing useful products for man. Man is the biological term this statement needs.

q: They can be cultured easily by using fermenters where they can reproduce profusely as they can be kept in optimum ____.
e: They can be cultured easily by using fermenters where they can reproduce profusely as they can be kept in optimum conditions. Conditions is the biological term this statement needs.

q: As they are not affected by outside conditions， like climate， they grow rapidly and can produce large amount of product in a short ____.
e: As they are not affected by outside conditions, like climate, they grow rapidly and can produce large amount of product in a short time. Time is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The nutrients they need are quite cheap and sometimes they can be fed with waste products of other industrial ____.
e: The nutrients they need are quite cheap and sometimes they can be fed with waste products of other industrial processes. Processes is the biological term this statement needs.

q: They are put to use in food technology， baking and brewing industries， in drug production， textile and mining， and production of biological washing powder and ____.
e: They are put to use in food technology, baking and brewing industries, in drug production, textile and mining, and production of biological washing powder and biofuel. Biofuel is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Raw or unrefined sugar obtained from sugarcane or cane wastes are used as nutrient for the anaerobically respiring ____.
e: Raw or unrefined sugar obtained from sugarcane or cane wastes are used as nutrient for the anaerobically respiring yeasts. Yeasts is the biological term this statement needs.

q: This fermentation process produces ethanol which is distilled to obtain pure ethanol. It is then mix with petrol to get ____ which is used for driving cars.
e: This fermentation process produces ethanol which is distilled to obtain pure ethanol. It is then mix with petrol to get gasohol which is used for driving cars. Fermentation is microbial chemical change of organic material, with or without oxygen in modern use. Yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: In Brazil， Zimbabwe and in USA some cars are already using ethanol and gasohol as energy sources and they cause less pollution than ____.
e: In Brazil, Zimbabwe and in USA some cars are already using ethanol and gasohol as energy sources and they cause less pollution than petrol. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: Biofuel can also be produced by using oil from rapeseeds or sunflower ____.
e: Biofuel can also be produced by using oil from rapeseeds or sunflower seeds. Seeds is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The single-celled fungi yeast is used in the making of ____.
e: The single-celled fungi yeast is used in the making of bread. In bread making, yeast produces carbon dioxide, which makes dough rise, plus ethanol. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel.

q: First flour， water， oil and yeasts are mixed together and ____ (folded and stretch repeatedly).
e: First flour, water, oil and yeasts are mixed together and kneaded (folded and stretch repeatedly). Kneaded is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Water activates the amylase enzymes to act on the starch in the flour breaking it down to ____.
e: Water activates the amylase enzymes to act on the starch in the flour breaking it down to sugar. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Amylase is the enzyme that hydrolyses starch.

q: Then the yeasts ferment (respire anaerobically) the sugar to carbon dioxide and ____.
e: Then the yeasts ferment (respire anaerobically) the sugar to carbon dioxide and ethanol. Yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: The dough is left to ferment at about 27 C for a few ____.
e: The dough is left to ferment at about 27 C for a few hours. Some stages of division are timed in hours in typical cell-cycle descriptions.

q: A sticky protein gluten holds the carbon dioxide gas bubbles in the dough and make it rise almost to twice of its original ____.
e: A sticky protein gluten holds the carbon dioxide gas bubbles in the dough and make it rise almost to twice of its original size. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: After that， the dough is baked in the oven at 200 C. Baking kills the yeasts and evaporates the ethanol and the expanding gas bubbles give the bread a light cellular ____.
e: After that, the dough is baked in the oven at 200 C. Baking kills the yeasts and evaporates the ethanol and the expanding gas bubbles give the bread a light cellular texture. Viruses are not cellular. Yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: Both yoghurt and cheese are made from ____.
e: Both yoghurt and cheese are made from milk. Milk is the biological term this statement needs.

q: First milk is pasteurized at about 90C degree to kill the bacteria in ____.
e: First milk is pasteurized at about 90C degree to kill the bacteria in it. It is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Then it is homogenized to break up the fat ____.
e: Then it is homogenized to break up the fat globules. Milk is homogenised to break up fat globules, not protein globules.

q: At 40C-45 C a starter culture of two species of bacteria ( Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus bulgaricus ) is added which turn the lactose， milk sugar， in milk to ____.
e: At 40C-45 C a starter culture of two species of bacteria (Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus bulgaricus) is added which turn the lactose, milk sugar, in milk to lactic acid. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: This acid coagulates the milk protein casein and thick creamy yoghurt is ____.
e: This acid coagulates the milk protein casein and thick creamy yoghurt is produced. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Casein is the main milk protein that clots in cheese making.

q: In the making of cheese the basic processes are the same as yoghurt. But after the coagulation of milk protein casein， a mixture of enzymes called ____ is added which causes further coagulation of the milk casein and solid lumps called curds are formed.
e: In the making of cheese the basic processes are the same as yoghurt. But after the coagulation of milk protein casein, a mixture of enzymes called rennet is added which causes further coagulation of the milk casein and solid lumps called curds are formed. Rennet enzymes clot casein during cheese making. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up.

q: The liquid whey is drained off and the solid curds are partially dried and ____.
e: The liquid whey is drained off and the solid curds are partially dried and compressed. Compressed is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Then the cheeses obtain are allowed to ripen and ____.
e: Then the cheeses obtain are allowed to ripen and mature. Mature is the biological term this statement needs.

q: To make wine， grapes are crushed and the extracted juice is placed in a large vessel or vat and treated with sulphur dioxide to kill the natural occurring ____.
e: To make wine, grapes are crushed and the extracted juice is placed in a large vessel or vat and treated with sulphur dioxide to kill the natural occurring yeast. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel. Wine yeast uses oxygen first, then ferments anaerobically when oxygen is gone.

q: A starter culture of yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is added which respire aerobically at first until the oxygen is used up .Then the yeast cells start to respire anaerobically fermenting the grape sugar (glucose) to alcohol and carbon ____.
e: A starter culture of yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is added which respire aerobically at first until the oxygen is used up.Then the yeast cells start to respire anaerobically fermenting the grape sugar (glucose) to alcohol and carbon dioxide. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel.

q: When the alcohol content reach 15%， the yeast cells die and the juice become ____.
e: When the alcohol content reach 15%, the yeast cells die and the juice become wine. Wine yeast uses oxygen first, then ferments anaerobically when oxygen is gone. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel.

q: Beer is made from barley ____.
e: Beer is made from barley grains. Grains is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The seeds are wetted and allowed to germinate thus activating the starch-digesting ____.
e: The seeds are wetted and allowed to germinate thus activating the starch-digesting enzymes. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Starch is the plant storage polysaccharide made of amylose and amylopectin.
